body:
We highlight five notable African private equity exits from 2026, as featured in our Dealmaker's Log, a database of reported investment deals, exits, and fundraising milestones. View the Dealmaker’s Log here

1. South Africa: EXEO Capital exits Chemical Process Technologies

EXEO Capital’s Agri-Vie Fund II has exited Chemical Process Technologies, a Pretoria-based manufacturer of active pharmaceutical ingredients for animal health, after a four-year hold. EXEO initially took a minority stake in 2022 before moving to majority control through additional growth capital.

2. Morocco: Amethis sells stake in logistics platform

Amethis has exited Globex, a Moroccan logistics and transport group. Founded in 1998 as a FedEx-licensed express delivery operator, Globex has grown into an integrated logistics provider covering freight forwarding, customs clearance, warehousing and road transport.

3. Helios lists T2S Group on Casablanca Stock Exchange

Helios Investment Partners has listed portfolio company T2S Group, an integrated med-tech group, on the Casablanca Stock Exchange in an offering that raised MAD 1.1 billion (about $120 million) at a post-money valuation of roughly MAD 4.9 billion ($520 million). Helios retained a 42% stake post-listing.

4. Capitalworks divests Minet to Adenia

Adenia Partners has acquired a majority stake in Minet Group, one of Africa’s largest independent insurance brokerage and risk advisory firms, from Capitalworks. Minet provides insurance broking, risk advisory and employee benefits services across nine African countries.

5. Eos Capital achieves 40% IRR from Namibian private equity exit

Eos Capital’s Allegrow Fund has exited The Mushara Collection, a group of private lodges near Etosha National Park, subject to regulatory approvals. The transaction delivered a 40% IRR and 4.4x return on invested capital.
